subject: forensic-medicine
title: Skull Fractures: Ring, Pond, Gutter and Contrecoup Injuries

steps.title: Fissured and comminuted fractures
steps.tx: A **fissured fracture** is a linear crack through the skull from a broad striking surface, while a **comminuted fracture** breaks bone into three or more fragments by two or more intersecting lines. Without displacement the comminuted pattern resembles a spider web or mosaic. Heavy iron bars, thick sticks, kicks and crushing vehicle injuries cause them. Fissured lines often radiate outward from a comminuted centre where the force landed.
steps.say: Linear cracks are fissured fractures, and three or more fragments in a spider web pattern make a comminuted fracture.

steps.title: Pond fractures only in infants
steps.tx: A **pond or indented fracture** is a simple dent in the skull, like a dent in a ping pong ball, produced by an obstetric forceps blade or a blunt impact against a protruding object. It occurs only in infant skulls. The inner table is not fractured, though the outer table may fissure around the dent's rim. The dura is not torn and the brain usually escapes damage, which separates pond fractures from depressed fractures of adults.
steps.say: Infant skulls dent like ping pong balls in pond fractures, sparing inner table, dura and brain in most cases.

steps.title: Gutter fractures from oblique bullets
steps.tx: When part of the skull thickness is scooped away by an oblique bullet, a **gutter fracture** results: a channel in the outer table with an irregular depressed fracture of the inner table beneath it. Dura and brain may be torn under the gutter. The pattern tells the examiner the bullet travelled tangentially rather than perforating, and the gutter's direction records the bullet's path across the head.
steps.say: An oblique bullet ploughs a gutter through the skull table, and the gutter points along its tangential path.

steps.title: Ring fracture around the foramen magnum
steps.tx: A **ring fracture** runs three to five centimetres outside the foramen magnum at the back and sides of the skull, separating the skull from the spine. It follows falls from a height onto the feet or buttocks, where force travels up the spinal column. A forceful blow on the chin in a traffic accident can also produce it through the jaw joints, usually without fracturing the mandible itself. Ring fractures are rare.
steps.say: Falling onto feet or buttocks can ring the foramen magnum and part skull from spine, and a chin blow can do the same.

steps.title: Base of skull fractures and CSF leaks
steps.tx: **Fractures of the skull base** arise by direct force at base level, general skull deformation, extension from the vault, or force transmitted through spine or face. Anterior fossa fractures bleed from nose and mouth; a torn cribriform plate with dura and nasal mucosa leaks cerebrospinal fluid and even brain into the nose, inviting leptomeningitis from ascending bacteria. Most basal lines converge on the pituitary fossa and open into basal foramina.
steps.say: Basal fractures leak blood and spinal fluid from the nose, and torn cribriform dura opens the road to meningitis.

steps.title: Coup injury at the point of impact
steps.tx: Damage directly beneath the blow is the **coup injury**: the skull bends inward at impact, contusing the cortex under it and sometimes fracturing into it. Coup lesions mark where force was applied, which is why their position reconstructs the direction of assault. A moving head striking a surface and a stationary head struck by a weapon both produce coup injury, though the accompanying patterns differ, as the next step shows.
steps.say: The bruise under the blow is the coup injury, and its site maps exactly where the force was applied.

steps.title: Contrecoup injury opposite the blow
steps.tx: When a moving head is suddenly arrested, the brain travels on and strikes the skull interior opposite the impact, producing **contrecoup injury** at the pole facing away from the blow. Local distortion of the skull and negative pressure at the opposite pole add to the damage. The line joining coup and contrecoup centres indicates the direction of force. Falls backward therefore tear the frontal and temporal poles against the rough anterior skull base.
steps.say: A falling head bruises the brain opposite the impact, so frontal pole damage follows a blow to the back of the head.

steps.title: Fractures that imitate weapon injury
steps.tx: Two mimics trap beginners. Small independent ossification centres leave **wormian bones** in the skull, and separation of one leaves an aperture easily mistaken for a weapon fracture. Sutural or diastatic fractures separate sutures, usually the sagittal, in young persons after blunt blows or raised intracranial pressure. Perforating fractures by contrast are clean holes from firearms, daggers or axes whose size matches the weapon cross section.
steps.say: A wormian bone gap imitates a fracture, suture separation marks young skulls, and clean holes match the weapon that punched them.

steps.title: Describing skull fractures for court
steps.tx: A court ready description records **type, site, direction and associated brain injury** for every fracture line. State whether lines radiate from a comminuted centre, whether fragments displaced into brain, and whether the base is involved with fluid leaks or nerve damage. Photograph before cleaning blood away, because clots hide entry wounds and fracture lines alike. The pattern as a whole often decides between fall, assault and firearm mechanisms.
steps.say: Record fracture type, radiation, displacement and base signs with photographs, because the whole pattern names the mechanism.
